item.description: DigitalCommons@UTEP (The University of Texas at El Paso) — As data increasingly shapes participation in society, there is growing emphasis on preparing youth to engage with data through computer science education. item.description: Environmental Innovation and Societal Transitions — In the current context of insufficient climate action and unmet demands for climate justice, civil society organizations are increasingly turning to the courts as part of a broader repertoire of strategies to accelerate ecological transitions and drive systemic change. This has contributed to a global surge in climate litigation, manifested through diverse legal arguments and associated campaigns. item.description: Geohazards & Remediation — Abstract Mass-movement disasters, including landslides, avalanches, and mudslides, are among the most critical types of geohazards influenced by climate variability and socio-economic exposure. A comprehensive global assessment linking long-term climate trends to mass-movement disasters and their socio-economic impacts remains limited, despite growing evidence of climate-driven intensification of geohazard frequency. item.title: A Mobile Phone-Based Mobility Dataset of Transient Populations During Hurricanes in Florida
item.description: Scientific Data — Transient populations—such as tourists, seasonal workers, and business travelers—are particularly vulnerable during hurricanes because they often lack familiarity with hazards, evacuation routes, communication channels, and social support networks. Despite their growing presence in disaster-prone regions such as Florida, their mobility behavior remains poorly documented due to limited fine-grained data. item.description: Journal of the European Meteorological Society. — Southern Europe is experiencing a shift towards a new wildfire regime, characterised by larger and more intense fires, and an extension of the fire season beyond the traditional summer months. Climate projections indicate that the occurrence and severity of fwildfires will increase faster than the global average due to an increased risk of heatwaves and droughts. item.description: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers — ABSTRACT In this paper, I propose a novel framework—‘affordabilities’, combining affordability, mobilities and affordances—to analyse the contingent construction of affordable lifestyles through interactions between relative inequalities and spatial relations. Through a focus on internal migration, I demonstrate that affordability is not an absolute quality confined to place or property, but plural and emergent through relative inequalities and relational spatial affordances. item.title: Integrating transport planning and infrastructure to reduce urban flood risk in Accra, Ghana
item.description: African Transport Studies — Accra's repeated urban flooding has been predominantly attributed to rainfall variability and inadequate drainage; however, the structural role of transport infrastructure influencing flood exposure remains empirically underexplored. This study examines the spatial and statistical relationships between transport infrastructure characteristics and flood occurrence across thirty road segments in the Accra Metropolitan Area (AMA), drawing on data from the National Disaster Management Organization (NADMO), the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet), and the Department of Urban Roads for the period 201

item.description: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research) — Urban-Grid (v5.2.0) is an open-source metropolitan infrastructure, transportation, and emergency-resilience simulator built to analyze everyday vehicle traffic, emergency-medical station placement, seismic bridge fragility, and disaster evacuation together on real city street maps. item.title: Interconnections of climate change, water scarcity, and conflict in shaping food security in the twenty-first century: a systematic review
item.description: Agriculture & Food Security — Food security in the twenty-first century is a complex challenge shaped by environmental, economic, social, and political factors beyond mere caloric availability. These challenges are particularly critical during political conflicts and emergencies, where disruptions to agricultural production, water systems, and food supply chains can intensify food insecurity. This systematic review aims to examine the interconnected effects of climate change, water scarcity, and conflict on food security and to provide a scientific framework for policymaking in emergency and conflict contexts. item.description: npj Climate Action — Abstract Extreme urban heat, amplified by the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, is a structural and recurring risk embedded within contemporary urban systems. Urban dwellers, especially those in low-income settings, outdoor workers, pregnant women, and other vulnerable groups, are disproportionately exposed to its health, economic, and social harms. item.description: Journal of Geophysical Research Atmospheres — Abstract This study investigated that the interannual covariation of Western Pacific Subtropical High (WPSH) and Indian Subtropical High (ISH) influences the biomass burning (BB) in the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) during the pre‐monsoon season (March–April). The analysis revealed that when the WPSH and ISH strengthen together, they tend to merge into an interconnected anticyclone that extends from the Indian Subcontinent to the South China Sea. item.description: Fronteiras Journal of Social Technological and Environmental Science — Sustainable development, as a political and pedagogical project, requires a critical articulation between environmental education, health, and public policies, understood as inseparable dimensions of social and environmental justice. In the Portuguese context, this articulation has been progressively incorporated into normative and strategic frameworks, in line with global sustainability agendas. item.title: Environmental pollution and associated health outcomes in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria
item.description: Discover Public Health — Crude oil exploration, gas flaring, and artisanal refining in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria are associated with human and environmental health deterioration. Their impact on environmental health encompasses the degradation of ecosystems through pollution and loss of biodiversity. Relating to human health, several pollution-related diseases and physiological dysfunctions have been documented. item.description: Brain Structure and Function — Abstract Fixel-based analysis (FBA) resolves fiber-specific white matter properties within crossing-fiber regions, where conventional diffusion tensor imaging is limited. We applied single-shell three-tissue constrained spherical deconvolution to diffusion MRI from 295 older adults in the Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project cohort, quantifying fiber density (FD), fiber-bundle cross-section (FC), and their composite (FDC) across the primary (N1), secondary (N2), and tertiary (N3) fiber populations within each white matter voxel. item.description: Agricultural Water Management — This study examines the relationships between selected natural and anthropogenic factors and agricultural productivity in 18 Sub-Saharan African countries over the period 1990–2020, using panel data from the FAOSTAT database. Agricultural productivity is measured as kilocalories produced per hectare of agricultural land. The explanatory variables include fertilizer use, agricultural water withdrawal, agricultural sector contribution to water stress, population, and agricultural land per capita. item.description: BMC Public Health — BACKGROUND: Housing quality as a key social determinant of health has received growing attention in public health research. Asylum seekers and refugees in European countries are frequently housed in institutionalized, camp-like facilities. These facilities are often characterized by overcrowding and limited privacy, safety, and autonomy. item.title: Valorisation of Bos-indicus excreta biowaste into nanocellulose-reinforced PVA composite films for sustainable seed coating
item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract Agro-livestock nano-composite film enhance bio-degradable polymeric property and seed coating technology. Nanocellulose derived from bovine excreta (BNC) offer a promising strategy for sustainable crop production and storage. In this study the optimized film was evaluated for dip seed coating i.e. mung bean (Vigna radiata). Nanocellulose-polyvinyl alcohol coated seeds showed significantly enhanced germination and seedling growth at 5% NC-PVA composite. After 6 days, root and shoot lengths reached 10.20 cm and 13.60 cm, respectively, compared with 6.95 and 9.85 cm for the H₂O control.

item.description: Scientific Reports — Climate change has profoundly altered global hydrological regimes and significantly intensified the occurrence of extreme flooding. Although discharge constitutes the dominant driver of flood genesis, flood propagation is also strongly controlled by channel and surface roughness conditions. item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract Retired pesticide sites are an important category of contaminated land, and groundwater pollution at these sites remains a major environmental concern. Understanding groundwater pollution characteristics and the effectiveness of containment measures is essential for site management and safe reuse. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. item.description: DS Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics — This manuscript examines the legal and ethical implications framework for the application of Artificial Intelligence in Ugandan Centenary banks, with a case study focus on the Lango Sub-Region of Northern Uganda. As banks increasingly deploy AI for credit scoring, fraud detection, customer onboarding, chatbots, anti-money laundering monitoring, and risk analytics, the technology promises greater efficiency, lower operating costs, and improved financial inclusion. item.description: Energy Systems — Abstract Large-scale technology transitions entail the simultaneous adoption of technologies and dependent resources, as well as a shift in policy and human capital. Systems often consist of multiple interdependent processes, allowing decisions to propagate through subsystems. item.description: Epilepsia — OBJECTIVE: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract Groundwater in the semi-arid Zagros foreland of northern Iraq is being withdrawn faster than it is replenished, and identifying where groundwater is most accessible is a precondition for managing that deficit. This study maps groundwater potential in the Karma Soor basin, Kurdistan Region, and compares three gradient-boosted ensemble learners, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost, tuned under identical settings with the Train Using AutoML tool in ArcGIS Pro. item.description: International Journal of Architectural Engineering Technology — Green building certification formally evaluates building performance, while it may not fully capture occupants’ experiences of indoor environmental quality (IEQ) during post-occupancy use. item.description: bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory) — Human papillomavirus-related (HPV+) cancers harbor a subset of tumor cells expressing certain senescence-related transcripts and reduced levels of HPV mRNAs. We aimed to define this HPV-low population′s biologic traits and clinical significance via integrated analysis of recurrence-prone human HPV+ oropharyngeal cancers (OPCs) and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) of variable therapy sensitivity. item.description: Island Studies Journal — The epistemologies based on the terra firma framework fall short in interpreting the relationship and transcendence of land and water concerning the river islands ( chars ). Consequently, the ways of life associated with these inhabited islands are also not considered along with the fluidities of its geography. item.title: The Insular and the Archipelagic: Epistemological Responsibility in Thinking With and From the Chiloé Archipelago
item.description: Island Studies Journal — The Chiloé Archipelago has been approached within island studies, yet its engagement with archipelagic thinking remains limited. This article seeks to ‘think with’ and ‘think from’ Chiloé, two notions central to recent debates in the field. Drawing on historical, ethnographical, essayistic, and mythological vignettes, I argue that Chiloé has come to be constituted as an archipelago through ‘insularization’. item.description: Journal of Research on Adolescence — School closures can disrupt not only educational access but also the relational and institutional conditions through which adolescents experience school belonging. This sequential mixed-methods study examined how COVID-19-related school closures reshaped school belonging among marginalized adolescent girls in rural India. item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — Bangladesh has one of the world's highest lightning death tolls, borne mostly by farmers and fishers, yet national hazard maps rest on interpolation or tabular machine learning without independent validation. item.title: Millipede abundance and diversity decline in response to megafires in Australian temperate rainforest
item.description: Insect Conservation and Diversity — Abstract Wildfires are increasing in severity, frequency and extent across many biomes. Litter invertebrates such as millipedes are diverse and functionally important in forests, but high‐severity fires incinerate their leaf litter habitat. In 2019–2020, ‘megafires’ burnt almost 10 million ha of vegetation in south‐eastern Australia, including large areas of temperate rainforest, which do not usually burn. item.description: Journal of Management and Administration Provision — The purpose of this study is to analyze disaster management policies, community adaptive capacity, and collaboration among government, local communities, and stakeholders in strengthening urban and community resilience to post-disaster conditions in Makassar City in a sustainable manner. This study employs a qualitative approach using in-depth interviews, field observations, document analysis, and focus group discussions (FGDs), with data analyzed using NVivo 12 Plus. item.title: From Environmental Exposure to Compound Vulnerability: Reframing Public Health Governance in Environmental Planning
item.description: Research Square — Abstract The effects of environmental determinants of public health have been investigated by individual pathways of exposure, including air pollution, unsafe water, climate stress, or waste exposure. This review discusses these risks in the light of the concept of compound vulnerabilities, which sees environmental health burdens as being not only determined by exposure, but also by governance, infrastructure, planning, social inequality and adaptive capacity. The study was carried out using a systematic review following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis.

item.description: Journal of Urban Health — Abstract Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. item.description: CACTUS — Airports have evolved from simple transit points into complex tourism gateways that shape the travel experience and generate significant non-aeronautical revenues. This study provides an innovative perspective by highlighting how each airport’s unique operating context affects the strategies available to airport managers for increasing non-aeronautical revenues while enhancing passenger satisfaction. item.description: Research Square — Abstract Larval connectivity underpins coral reef persistence, yet genetic and biophysical modelling approaches are rarely integrated. item.title: Have we already lost it? Geoprivacy in the age of AI, uncertainty, and corporate gatekeeping
item.description: Computers Environment and Urban Systems — Geoprivacy is often framed as a problem of protecting coordinates, masking traces, or managing user consent. This framing is now insufficient. In an era of pervasive datafication, AI-enabled inference, platform dependence, and corporate control over location and mobility data, the central question is no longer whether exact locations can be hidden, but whether meaningful control over location-derived knowledge remains possible at all.
